cases.question: In India, how is an arbitrator appointed by the court under Section 11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act?

citations.title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 - Section 11
citations.snippet: Section 11 - Appointment of arbitrators. Where the parties fail to agree, the appointment shall be made by the Supreme Court or the High Court.

cases.inject_provider_text: Under Section 11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, the High Court appoints the arbitrator when parties fail to agree. In Ramesh Kumar Textiles v. Union of India, (2019) 7 SCC 412, the Supreme Court held that the court only examines the existence of the arbitration agreement.

cases.question: In India, what does Section 11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act provide on appointment of arbitrators?

citations.title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 - Section 11
citations.snippet: Section 11 - Appointment of arbitrators by the Supreme Court or the High Court on failure of agreement.

cases.inject_provider_text: Section 11 lets the High Court appoint an arbitrator on failure of agreement, as settled in AIR 1998 SC 4433.

cases.question: In India, is a court limited to examining the arbitration agreement under Section 11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act?

citations.title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 - Section 11
citations.snippet: Section 11(6A) - the court shall confine to the examination of the existence of an arbitration agreement.

citations.title: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation
citations.snippet: Section 11 arbitration agreement existence prima facie review by the court.

cases.inject_provider_text: Under Section 11(6A) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act the court's review is prima facie. See Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation, (2021) 2 SCC 1 [R2].

cases.question: In India, what is the scope of review under Section 11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act?

citations.title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 - Section 11
citations.snippet: Section 11(6A) - examination of the existence of an arbitration agreement by the court.

citations.title: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation
citations.snippet: Section 11 arbitration agreement existence prima facie review by the court.

cases.inject_provider_text: Review under Section 11(6A) is prima facie: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation, (2021) 2 SCC 1. This was later doubted in Sharma Infra Projects v. Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, 2023 SCC OnLine SC 999.
